metas.name: Infrastructure - 29 in Ad Dhakhiliyah
metas.note: The southern section of Road 29 only has a middle white line, which along with the greyish and sandy desert landscape makes this road unique.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (divided)
metas.note: The divided section of Road 31 is the only divided road going through a flat desert landscape.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (single lane)
metas.note: This long stretch of Road 31 can be recognised by the light-coloured flat desert landscape along with the wide shoulders and the often faded road lines. The weather is usually somewhat cloudy.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 37 (Powerline)
metas.note: Road 37 travels in a generally northwest direction through a very generic, flat desert landscape. The angle is one of the best clues for this road. On the southern half, a big power line is visible to the northeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (flat)
metas.note: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (hilly)
metas.note: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders. The western parts can get quite hilly

metas.name: Infrastructure - 42 north of Shalim
metas.note: North of Shalim Road 42 turns into a very wide unpaved road, with the soil being quite light in colour. You’ll sometimes see oil drills in the distance along this stretch.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Black
metas.note:
Black Bins can be found everywhere except for Batina North. They're also rarely found in South-Dhakiliyah.

NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Grey
metas.note:
Grey Bins can be found in Dharihar, South Dhakhiliyah, Dhofar, Bathina North and west of Muscat.

NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / Black Sticker
metas.note: Black bins with a black sticker on the front can be found in Al Buraimi, Ash Sharqiyah North, and Muscat Governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / No Sticker
metas.note:
Black bins without stickers are mainly found in Al Batinah South Governorate and north of Al Khaburah in Al Batinah North Governorate.

NOTE: Black bins throughout Oman may appear like they lack stickers, so use this with caution.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / White Sticker
metas.note: Black bins with a white sticker are found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, southern Dhofar Governorate, and Muscat Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Western Bin
metas.note: Western-style small black bins are found in Muscat and eastern Al Batinah North Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chevron Bin
metas.note:
Bins in Muscat governorate often have white-and-red chevron-like stickers on the sides.

Note by MB: 'often' really is an overstatement, definitely don't rule Muscat out if you don't have those stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Fahud Road
metas.note: The road west of Fahud goes through a flat desert with pink-greyish soil. The road itself is in poor shape and without roadlines as well as the direction of the road being southeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / Black Sticker
metas.note: Grey bins with a black sticker on the front are found in Ad Dhahirah Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / No Sticker
metas.note:
Grey bins without a sticker on the front are found in Al Batinah North Governorate.

NOTE: They can have a sticker on the side.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / White Sticker
metas.note: Grey bins with a white sticker are commonly found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, and sometimes in Dhofar Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ibri Road
metas.note: The road going to Saudi Arabia from Ibri can be recognised by the completely flat desert landscape with bright pink-greyish soil along with the road having very wide shoulders and the overall great road condition. The southern portion goes in a straight northeast direction, and the northern section curves more and can have more shrubs.

metas.name: Infrastructure - North of Ubar Road
metas.note: The unlabelled road northwest of Ubar can be recognised by the small white markings between the dashes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oil Drills
metas.note: Oil drills are common around Amal and sometimes seen along Road 39.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road to Yemen
metas.note: Just west of ميتان, only labelled in Arabic on Google Maps, literally translating to methane, there is a stretch of road, which has a uniquely light-coloured pavement. To the north, you can see sand dunes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road west of Ubar
metas.note: West of Ubar, the 43 and the unlabelled road west of it are still unpaved but now have a power line to the north. The desert landscape has an orange tint to it.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Side Sticker
metas.note: Regardless of colour, if the bins have a sticker on the side, you should be in one of the North Coast governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - South-East of Ubar Road
metas.note:
The road southeast of Ubar has a general northwest bound angle, along with a power line to the left of the road. You will often see signs of life in the form of farms or buildings on this road.

NOTE: Don’t mix this up with the 37, which has a similar angle, but is more desolate and can have sunset coverage.

metas.name: Landscape - 35
metas.note: Road 35 is surrounded by hills and mountains, and the ground is mostly covered in green shrubs. Curved lamp posts are posted at regular intervals on the northeastern side of the road.

metas.name: Landscape - 45 south of Mudayy
metas.note: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Adam Ridge
metas.note: Just north of Adam, you’ll find a flat desert landscape with greyish soil and mountains in the distance, notably one long ridge to the south followed by two smaller and rounder hills to the east and southeast. Other mountains are also visible to the north and west.

metas.name: Landscape - Al Amarat
metas.note: If you are surrounded by mountains on all sides, and you are in a somewhat urban area, you are likely just southeast of Muscat, in Al Amarat.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Dunes
metas.note: South of Bidiyah you can find a couple of dirt roads going through a slightly rolling landscape consisting of orange-pink sand and small yellow-ish shrubs. The roads mainly go between long and low sand dunes with a general south-south-west direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Flat
metas.note: Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41
metas.note: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41 - Ridge
metas.note: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance. On the north-to-south stretch, you can see a distant ridge to the west.

metas.name: Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.note: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah - 51
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Max South 45
metas.note: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Musandam
metas.note: Most of the coverage in the Musandam Governorate exclave is coastal, with rocky cliffs usually hugging the road. A majority, but not all, of this coverage will have the coast to the west, excluding any other roads in the country with a similar look.

metas.name: Landscape - Narrow 32
metas.note: Going further north, Road 32 travels through a hilly desert landscape, in a general northern direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Nizwa Mountains
metas.note: The mountains north of Nizwa have an amount of green bushes that are unusually large for the north. The mountains are very rocky and jagged, which differentiates them from the more rolling mountains in the south.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Awaya Road
metas.note: The road north of Al Awaya features a desert landscape with dark grey soil, which is not common in the south. The road itself still has the orange tint characteristic of southwest Oman.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Mazyunah Road
metas.note: The unpaved road north of Al Mazyunah, near the Yemen border, has a north-north-west bound angle, and the desert has sandy, red-tinted sand, which still has some shrubbery around. You can see some hills in the distance. The southwards driving direction and sunny weather can be used as confirmation.

metas.name: Landscape - Orange Sanddunes
metas.note:
A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.

NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.

metas.name: Landscape - Rolling Hills
metas.note: Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.

metas.name: Landscape - Sadah Coastal Road
metas.note: Road 42/49 east of Salalah is a scenic coastal road that features a lot of light-coloured tall rocky cliffs. The coast is also often visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Salalah Plains
metas.note: Salalah is located on a flat coastal plain with rolling mountains surrounding it to the north.

metas.name: Landscape - Ubar Fields
metas.note: Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.

metas.name: Landscape - Western 41
metas.note: The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart.

metas.name: Landscape - Wide 32
metas.note: Crossing into the Ash Sharqiyah North Governorate, the shoulders become wide, like those on Road 31. However, unlike Road 31, the desert here is darker and has more shrubs and greenery. A long portion of the road also has overcast coverage. The lighter red section is no longer road 32 but still features the wide shoulders. The landscape further north also gets hillier and more vegetated.

metas.name: Vegetation - Acacia
metas.note: Acacia trees, recognisable by their relatively short height and umbrella-like flat crowns, are most abundant and common in northern Oman, but can also be found close to the rest of the coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Coconut Palm
metas.note: Coconut palms are usually found near Salalah.

metas.name: Vegetation - Date Palm
metas.note: Date palm plantations are most common along the northern coast.
